'''''Acer palmatum''''', commonly known as '''Japanese maple''',<ref>{{PLANTS|id=ACPA2|taxon=Acer palmatum|access-date=6 January 2016}}</ref> '''palmate maple''',<ref>{{Cite book|url=http://www.forest.go.kr/kna/special/download/English_Names_for_Korean_Native_Plants.pdf |title=English Names for Korean Native Plants |publisher=[[Korea National Arboretum]] |year=2015 |isbn=978-89-97450-98-5 |location=Pocheon |page=334 |access-date=25 January 2016 |via=[[Korea Forest Service]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170525105020/http://www.forest.go.kr/kna/special/download/English_Names_for_Korean_Native_Plants.pdf |archive-date=25 May 2017 }}</ref> or '''smooth Japanese maple'''<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |access-date=2014-10-17 }}</ref> (Korean: ''danpungnamu'' [{{lang|ko|단풍나무}}]; Japanese: ''irohamomiji'' [{{Nihongo2|イロハモミジ}}] or ''momiji'' [{{lang|ja|紅葉}}]), is a species of woody plant native to [[Korea]], [[Japan]], [[China]], eastern [[Mongolia]], and far eastern [[Russia]].<ref name=grin>{{GRIN | access-date = 11 December 2017}}</ref> Many different [[cultivar]]s of this [[maple]] have been selected and they are grown worldwide for their large variety of attractive forms, leaf shapes, and spectacular colors.<ref>Philips, Roger (1979). ''Trees of North America and Europe''. New York: [[Random House]]. {{ISBN|0-394-50259-0}}.</ref>

== Description ==
''Acer palmatum'' is [[deciduous]], with the growth habit of a [[shrub]] or small [[tree]] reaching heights of {{convert|6|to|10|m|ft|abbr=on}}{{Citation needed|date=September 2025}}, rarely {{cvt|16|m}}{{Citation needed|date=September 2025}}, reaching a mature width of {{cvt|4.5|to|10|m}},<ref>{{Cite web|title=Japanese maple | website = The [[Morton Arboretum]] |url=https://www.mortonarb.org/trees-plants/tree-plant-descriptions/japanese-maple|access-date=2020-07-20}}</ref> often growing as an understory plant in shady [[woodland]]s in its native habitat. It may have multiple trunks joining close to the ground. In [[Habit (biology)|habit]], its canopy often takes on a [[dome]]-like form, especially when mature.<ref name="gelderen">van Gelderen, C.J. & van Gelderen, D.M. (1999). ''Maples for Gardens: A Color Encyclopedia''.</ref> The [[leaf|leaves]] are {{cvt|4|–|12|cm|in |frac=4}} long and wide, palmately lobed with five, seven, or nine acutely pointed lobes. The [[flower]]s are produced in small [[Cyme (botany)|cymes]], the individual flowers with five red or purple sepals and five whitish petals. The [[fruit]] is a pair of winged [[samara (fruit)|samaras]], each samara {{cvt|2|–|3|cm|in |frac=4}} long with a {{cvt|6|–|8|mm|in |frac=16}} seed. The seeds of ''Acer palmatum'' and similar [[species]] require [[stratification (botany)|stratification]] in order to [[germinate]].<ref name="gelderen"/><ref name=rushforth>Rushforth, K. (1999). ''Trees of Britain and Europe''. Collins {{ISBN|0-00-220013-9}}.</ref>

Even in nature, ''Acer palmatum'' displays considerable [[genetic variation]], with [[seedling]]s from the same parent tree typically showing differences in such traits as leaf size, shape, and color.  The overall form of the tree can vary from upright to weeping.<ref name="gelderen"/>

Three [[subspecies]] are recognised:<ref name="gelderen"/><ref name=rushforth/>
* ''Acer palmatum'' subsp. ''palmatum''. Leaves small, {{cvt|4|–|7|cm|in |frac=4}} wide, with five or seven lobes and double-serrate margins; seed wings {{cvt|10|–|15|mm|in |frac=8}}. Lower altitudes throughout central and southern Japan (not [[Hokkaido]]).
* ''Acer palmatum'' subsp. ''amoenum'' {{small|(Carrière) H.Hara}}. Leaves larger, {{cvt|6|–|12|cm|in |frac=4}} wide, with seven or nine lobes and single-serrate margins; seed wings {{cvt|20|–|25|mm|in |frac=8}}. Higher altitudes throughout Japan and South Korea.
* ''Acer palmatum'' subsp. ''matsumurae'' {{small|Koidz}}. Leaves larger, {{cvt|6|–|12|cm|in |frac=4}} wide, with seven (rarely five or nine) lobes and double-serrate margins; seed wings {{cvt|15|–|25|mm|in |frac=8}}. Higher altitudes throughout Japan.

==Cultivation and uses==

[[File:Maples leaves and lantern.jpg|thumb|[[Shimogamo Shrine|Shimogamo-jinja]]|alt=Leaves at [[Shimogamo Shrine|Shimogamo-jinja]]]]
[[File:Arashiyama Hanatōro, Nison-in 嵐山花灯路・二尊院 紅葉と月 DSCF5361.JPG|thumb|[[Nison-in]]|alt=Leaves, [[Nison-in]]]]
[[File:2014-11-24 Sekiganji 石龕寺 DSCF4738.jpg|thumb|In [[Japan]], people have long admired the gradation of colors of the leaves during the autumn foliage season.]]
''Acer palmatum'' has been cultivated in Japan for centuries and in [[temperate zone|temperate]] areas around the world since the 1800s.<ref name="gelderen"/> The first specimen of the tree reached Britain in 1821.

When Swedish doctor-botanist [[Carl Peter Thunberg]] traveled in Japan late in the eighteenth century, he produced drawings of a small tree that would eventually become synonymous with the high art of oriental gardens.<ref>{{cite web |title=History of Japanese Maples and Value as a Landscaping Tree |website=Arbor Day Foundation |url=http://www.arborday.org/shopping/trees/japaneseredmaple/history.cfm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100425083322/http://www.arborday.org/shopping/trees/japaneseredmaple/history.cfm |archive-date=April 25, 2010 }}</ref> He gave it the species name ''palmatum'' after the hand-like shape of its leaves, similar to the centuries-old Japanese names ''kaede'' and ''momiji'', references to the 'hands' of frogs<ref>{{cite web |url=http://gogen-allguide.com/ka/kaede.html |title=Etymology of 楓 [Maple] |date=24 October 2005 |language=ja |quote=[The word ''kaede'' derives from ''kaeru te'' "frog hand" and went through the intermediary form ''kaende'']}}</ref> and babies,{{Citation needed|date=November 2010}} respectively.

Japanese horticulturalists have long developed [[cultivars]] from maples found in Japan and nearby Korea and China. They are a popular choice for [[bonsai]]<ref name="Ma-Ke_Acer palmatum ">{{cite web | last=D'Cruz | first=Mark | title=Acer palmatum Bonsai Care Guide | publisher=Ma-Ke Bonsai | url=http://makebonsai.com/guide/bonsailink.asp?quicklink=5021&name=Acer_palmatum | access-date=2010-11-26 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100617131223/http://www.makebonsai.com/guide/bonsailink.asp?quicklink=5021&name=Acer_palmatum | archive-date=17 June 2010 }}</ref> enthusiasts and have long been a subject in art.

Numerous cultivars are popular in [[Europe]] and [[North America]], with red-leafed favored, followed by cascading green shrubs with deeply dissected leaves.<ref name="gelderen"/>

''Acer palmatum'' includes thousands of named cultivars with a variety of forms, colors, leaf types, sizes, and preferred growing conditions. Heights of mature specimens range from 0.5 to 25 m (1 <sup>1</sup>⁄<sub>2</sub> to 82 ft), depending on type.

Preparations from the branches and leaves are used as a treatment in [[traditional Chinese medicine]].<ref>{{cite web |title=''Acer palmatum'' Thunb. |url=http://libproject.hkbu.edu.hk/was40/detail?lang=en&channelid=1288&searchword=herb_id=D00973 |website=School of Chinese Medicine database |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303222705/http://libproject.hkbu.edu.hk/was40/detail?lang=en&channelid=1288&searchword=herb_id%3DD00973 |archive-date=March 3, 2016 |publisher=Hong Kong Baptist University }}</ref> The leaves are edible; a local dish originating from [[Minoh]], ''momiji [[tempura]]'', involves [[pickling]] the leaves for a year before coating them in flour, sesame seeds and sugar, then [[deep frying]] them.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Soulhub |date=2020-09-11 |title=Momiji Tempura: Taking a bite out of Autumn |url=https://soulhub.co.uk/momiji-tempura-taking-a-bite-out-of-autumn/ |access-date=2025-07-12 |website=Soulhub |language=en-US}}</ref>

===Growing conditions===

[[File:Acer palmatum BotGartenMuenster Faecherahorn 6691.jpg|thumb|This mature specimen displays the characteristic dome-like canopy.]]

In their natural habitat, they grow in the understory; most cultivars prefer part shade, especially in hotter climates, but they will also grow in heavy shade. Some cultivars will tolerate full sun, more so at higher latitudes and less at lower latitudes; red, purple-red, black-red, bronze, and some dark green cultivars are generally more full sun tolerant.  Variegated white, cream, yellow, yellow-orange, or light green cultivars mostly require shade protection.  Almost all are adaptable and blend well with [[companion plant]]s. The trees are particularly suitable for borders and ornamental paths because the root systems are compact and not invasive.  Many varieties of ''Acer palmatum'' are successfully grown in containers.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2022-01-19|title=Japanese Maple: How To Grow It In Pots|url=https://lawnpundit.com/grow-japanese-maple-pot/|access-date=2022-02-08|website=LawnPundit.com|language=en-US|archive-date=8 February 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220208125258/https://lawnpundit.com/grow-japanese-maple-pot/}}</ref><ref>Vertrees, J.D. (1987) ''Japanese Maples''. Timber Press, Inc. {{ISBN|0-88192-048-7}}</ref>  Trees are prone to die during periods of drought and prefer consistent water conditions; more established trees are less prone to drought. Moderate to well-drained soil is essential as they will not survive in poorly drained waterlogged soil. Trees do not require heavy fertilization and should only be very lightly fertilized.

Japanese maples are best to grow in hardiness zones 5–8.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Acer palmatum - Thunb. |url=https://pfaf.org/user/Plant.aspx?LatinName=Acer+palmatum |access-date=7 April 2023 |website=[[Plants for a Future]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-10-08 |title=How to Select the Right Japanese Maple for Your Garden |url=https://www.monrovia.com/be-inspired/how-to-select-the-right-japanese-maple.html |access-date=2023-04-07 |website=www.monrovia.com |language=en}}</ref>

===Pruning===
{{See also|Bonsai|}}

[[File:Acer palmatum img.jpg|right|thumb|upright|Fall, [[Nara, Japan|Nara]]]]

If space is not a constraint, no pruning is necessary except to remove any dead branches.  Trees naturally self-prune foliage that doesn't receive enough light, such as internal branches which are overly shaded by its own canopy.  Some growers prefer to shape their trees artistically or to thin out interior branches to better expose the graceful main branches. The form of the tree, especially without leaves in winter, can be of great interest and can be pruned to highlight this feature.  Trees heal readily after pruning without needing aftercare.  This species should not be pruned like a hedge, but instead methodically shaped by carefully choosing individual branches to remove.  They can also be pruned just to maintain a smaller size to suit a particular location. ''Acer palmatum'' can also be used as [[espalier]].{{citation needed|date=March 2023}}

===Cultivars===
{{Refimprove section|date=March 2025}}
[[File:Acer-palmatum-ssp.jpg|thumb|left|upright=2|Various cultivars|alt=Examples of leaf variation among 4 cultivars]]

Over 1,000 [[cultivar]]s have been chosen for particular characteristics, which are [[plant propagation|propagated]] by asexual reproduction most often by [[grafting]], but some cultivars can also be propagated by [[Shield budding|budding]], [[Vegetative reproduction|cuttings]], [[tissue culture]], or [[layering (horticulture)|layering]]. Some cultivars are not in cultivation in the [[Western world]] or have been lost over the generations, but many new cultivars are developed each decade.<ref name="gelderen"/> Cultivars are chosen for [[phenotype|phenotypical]] aspects such as leaf shape and size (shallowly to deeply lobed, some also palmately compound), leaf color (ranging from chartreuse through dark green or from orange to red, to dark purple, others [[variegated]] with various patterns of white and pink), bark texture and color, and growth pattern. Most cultivars are less vigorous and smaller than is typical for the species, but are more interesting than the relatively mundane species.  Cultivars come in a large variety of forms including upright, broom, vase, umbrella, weeping, cascading, dwarf, shrub, and ground cover.  Most cultivars are [[artificially selected]] from seedlings of open-pollinated plants, purposeful breeding is not common, and less often from grafts of [[witch's broom]]s.

In Japan, ''iromomiji'' is used as an accent tree in Japanese gardens, providing gentle shade next to the house in the summer and beautiful colors in autumn. Many cultivars have characteristics that come into prominence during different seasons, including the color of new or mature leaves, extraordinary autumn color, color and shape of samaras, or even bark that becomes more brightly colored during the winter. Some cultivars can scarcely be distinguished from others unless labeled. In some cases, identical cultivars go by different names, while in other cases, different cultivars may be given the same name.

| title = ''Acer palmatum'' 'Shish geshira'
| publisher = RHS | access-date = 27 February 2020}}</ref>
* 'Skeeter's Broom'; derived from a 'Bloodgood' witch's broom
* 'Tamukeyama'; finely dissected, dark purple, cascading habit
* 'Trompenburg'; {{smallcaps|agm}}<ref>{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Acer palmatum'' 'Trompenburg'|url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/26157/Acer-palmatum-Trompenburg-(M)/Details | access-date=23 February 2020 | publisher = [[Royal Horticultural Society]] (RHS) }}</ref>  slender, upright grower, convex lobes, purple leaves
* 'Tsuma gaki'; yellow leaves with reddish-purple borders
* 'Villa Taranto'; {{smallcaps|agm}}<ref>{{cite web
| url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/92504/Acer-palmatum-Villa-Taranto-(L)/Details
| title=''Acer palmatum'' 'Villa Taranto' (L)
 | publisher = [[Royal Horticultural Society]] (RHS)
| access-date=2 March 2020}}</ref>
* 'Yuba e'; upright tree with scarlet variegation

In addition to the cultivars described above, a number of [[cultivar group]]s have been naturally selected over time to such an extent that seedlings often resemble the parent. Many of these are sold under the same name as the cultivars, or even propagated by grafting, so there is often much ambiguity in distinguishing them.<ref name="gelderen"/> In particular, a number of dark-red ''Acer palmatum'' are sold with the names 'Atropurpureum' and 'Bloodgood'. Many different cultivars with delicate lace-like foliage are sold under names such as 'Dissectum', 'Filigree' and 'Laceleaf'.<ref name="gelderen"/>

===Similar species===
The term "Japanese maple" is also sometimes used to describe other species, usually within the [[series (botany)|series]] ''Palmata'', that are similar to ''A. palmatum'' and native to China, Korea or Japan, including:{{citation needed|date=March 2023}}
* ''[[Acer duplicatoserratum]]'' (syn. ''A. palmatum'' var. ''pubescens'' Li)
* ''[[Acer japonicum]]''—downy Japanese maple
* ''[[Acer pseudosieboldianum]]''—Korean maple
* ''[[Acer shirasawanum]]''—fullmoon maple
* ''[[Acer sieboldianum]]''—Siebold's maple
* ''[[Acer buergerianum]]''—trident maple
* ''[[Acer circinatum]]—vine maple'' 
Given that these maples are phenotypically variable within each species, and may [[Hybrid (biology)|hybridise]] with one another, distinguishing between them may be a matter of [[speciation|gradient speciation]]. In commercial propagation, ''A. palmatum'' is often used as [[rootstock]] for many of these other species.<ref name="gelderen"/>
